summary: The Surge to Save Newborns Act amends the Public Health Service Act to create a special grant program for States. The goal of the program is to help States timely implement newborn screenings for conditions included on the recommended uniform screening panel maintained by the Secretary.

affected_groups.effect: State health officers or governmental agencies can apply for and receive grant funding to implement newborn screenings for recommended conditions.
May experience timelier implementation of newborn screening for conditions on the recommended uniform screening panel.

key_provisions: Establishes a grant program for States to implement timely newborn screenings for conditions on the Secretary's recommended uniform screening panel.
Requires grant applicants to be a State's chief executive officer for health (or designee) or a State governmental agency.
Requires grant applicants to submit an application describing how they plan to use the funds for newborn screening implementation.
Mandates annual reports to Congress from fiscal year 2027 through fiscal year 2031 detailing State-by-State newborn screening implementation, grant effectiveness, and recommendations.
Appropriates $35,000,000 annually from the Treasury for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2031 to fund the grants.
missing_information: Specific details on the exact grant application procedures and timelines required by the Secretary.
The complete list of conditions currently on or planned for the recommended uniform screening panel referenced in the bill text.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Surge to Save Newborns Act amends the Public Health Service Act to create a special grant program for States. The goal of the program is to help States timely implement newborn screenings for conditions included on the recommended uniform screening panel maintained by the Secretary.
summary_detail.significance: The bill provides federal grant funding of $35 million per year from fiscal years 2027 through 2031 to support States in implementing newborn screening tests.
